events.title: Protection Charm With Traditional Korean Patchwork
events.description: These classes center on the theme, "The Art of Being With...," and are related to the exhibit at Minneapolis Central Library. Together, they explore the idea that giving and receiving care and love brings meaning to our lives. Thoughtfulness is essential in finding purpose; without it, everyday moments can feel less significant. Rather than focusing on technical skills, each class highlights the meaningful act of creating objects that reflect care. Participants will work with ceramic painting and traditional textile elements to practice thoughtfulness and express care for themselves and others. No previous experience is needed; all skill levels are welcome. In session one of the two-part series, participants will paint and work with textiles. In session two, textile work will be incorporated and ceramic pieces will be painted and assembled into the finished object. Materials provided. Register for both sessions. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund. September 12 : Painting on ceramic pollack + sewing Jogakbo. Cultural significance: In a custom called Bugeo Aekmaegi, dried pollack uses its wide-open eyes and mouth to watch for evil spirits and swallow misfortune. This is paired with Jogakbo (patchwork), the traditional Korean art of "wrapping luck" and fortune. September 26 : Painting on ceramic old coin + sewing Jogakbo. Cultural significance: These represent Byeoljeon, rare commemorative coins gifted by mothers to marrying daughters on decorative key pendants to wish for marital harmony and prosperity. This is paired with Jogakbo patchwork to wrap and hold that family fortune together. View The Art of Being With: Light, Shadow, Wind and Body exhibit – on display August 8-September 27 in Cargill Gallery on the second floor of Minneapolis Central Library.

events.description: Learn about the fish people like to catch in the area and make a fishing rig out of a pop can. All ages welcome!  Meet in front of the Interpretive/Visitor Center. The building is closed due to construction. All programs will take place outdoors. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.

events.title: Nature Table: Plants Before Flowers - A Journey Through Plant Evolution
events.description: Come visit with a naturalist intern to explore interesting plant adaptations through time, focusing on different groups of plants that grow in the area.  Look for the Naturalist in the Beach Area between 12:30 - 2:30 p.m. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.

events.title: Nature Table: Plants Before Flowers - A Journey Through Plant Evolution

Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.

events.title: Written in Stone
events.description: It's not just a rock - it's a clue!  Rocks hold the secrets of the earth, trapping clues of time and place as they form.  Millions of years later we can use these clues to discover ancient worlds that used to exist right here at St. Croix State Park.

events.title: Exploration Station: Pollinator Party
events.description: Drop by the Pollinator Habitat buzzing with excitement. Find Naturalist Mic among the plant beings in the garden area outside the visitor center. Make your own insect inspired by what you find around you. Visit the information table for resources on providing habitat at home or in your community.  If it is raining, stop by the theater inside the visitor center.  Free parking is available in the Wayside Rest lot. This lot is located next to the visitor center.

events.title: Guardians of the Garden
events.description: At the pollinator garden by the Swinging Bridge. Discover how the park's wildflowers rely on bees, butterflies, and other pollinators to thrive. We'll explore the hidden connection between blooms and the creatures that help them grow. Stop in to chat with the naturalist about what's buzzing around our pollinator garden today.

events.title: Mysteries in History: The Picnic Grounds
events.description: Meet at the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds. Have you ever had a picnic in Itasca State Park�s picnic grounds and wondered who had eaten a meal in the same place? What would their view have been? Who would they have seen? What kinds of activities could they have done nearby after lunch? Come along on a hike through this area to visualize and learn more about the buildings both past and present, the previous residents, and how the area came to be the picnic grounds.

events.title: Pigeon River Phenology Hike
events.description: Pigeon River Phenology Hike Join us for a guided walk along the Pigeon River as we explore the seasonal changes taking place in the natural world. This adult-focused phenology hike will highlight blooming plants, emerging insects, and the wildlife that inhabits the river corridor, including birds, beavers, fish, and other animals that make their home along the river. Along the way, we'll also learn about the Grand Portage Ojibwe and their enduring relationship with this landscape. We'll explore how the region's geology, waterways, forests, and plant communities have supported life for generati

events.title: Discovery Table - Terrific Tracking!
events.description: Who walked this trail before you? Stop by the Discovery Table to become a wildlife detective!   The table is set up outside in front of the River Inn Visitor Center.  In case of rain, the table will move indoors.

events.title: Discovery Table - Aquatic Wonders Trivia
events.description: Dive into the ultimate aquatic challenge! Spin the wheel and answer a question about the plants and animals of the river, the Swinging Bridge, or anything water related. The table is set up outside the River Inn Visitor Center.

events.title: Kids Explorer Club Nature Hike
events.description: Kids Explorer Club: Nature Hike Adventure Join us for a fun outdoor adventure with the Kids Explorer Club! As we walk along the Pigeon River, we'll use our binoculars and dip nets to explore the wonders of nature. We'll look for birds, insects, wildflowers, and seek out river water creatures along the shoreline. Along the way, we'll practice our observation skills by listening, watching, and discovering the amazing plants and animals that live around us. Bring your walking shoes and a sense of adventure!

events.title: Birding for Beginners
events.description: How many times have you seen a bird flying by and wondered what kind of bird it was?  How many species of birds can be seen in Minnesota, or you would like to use a binocular but couldn't figure how to find that hopping bird through it?  It is Spring and many birds are back or passing by.  Come with Fort Snelling State Park's naturalist for a guided bird watching adventure.  Learn the correct techniques of using binoculars and how to adjust binoculars to fit your preference.  We will show you how to identify some of the common bird species from their calls and appearances.  Bird watching is a

events.title: Our Great Northern Diver: Tackling Threats to the Common Loon
events.description: Take a dive- deep into the underwater world of the Common Loon. At this exciting sit-down program, you will be dazzled with the skills of loons and how these birds are designed to dive deep and what threats they face in our lakes. Learn how to tackle these threats today!  Located at the outdoor amphitheater by Lady Slipper Lodge. Appropriate for all ages.

events.title: Bats Eat Bugs (great for all ages)
events.description: 2026 is Bat Year at Wild River State Park. Join the naturalist for a special program with activities, games and stories that celebrate the eight species of bats in Minnesota. We'll take a twenty-minute bat walk in the middle of the program on a flat, paved trail. This program is designed for kids and adults.     Meet at the visitor center at the start time. Seating is available.

events.title: Fishing Friday Afternoons
events.description: Let's go fishing!  Join us as we learn all about fishing ... identifying species, casting, and more.  We provide the poles, bait and instructors. Minnesota residents do not need a fishing license for this activity. Meet in the picnic area, across the parking lot from the Interpretive Center.  The Interpretive/Visitor Center is closed due to construction. All programs will take place outdoors. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: St. Croix Sunrise
events.description: Join us to experience the park at daybreak as the sun rises across the St. Croix River and dawn creatures stir. What is it that makes this time of day special?  What changes does the morning bring to the world around us?  Bring a picnic blanket or a camp chair and get ready to explore nature in the wee hours of the day. Flashlight and bug spray recommended. Meet at the St. Croix Lodge.  We will then walk down to the Main Canoe Landing in the campground area.

events.description: Join Park Naturalist Mic, on a tour of Gooseberry Falls State Park's major waterfalls, in the most adaptive way possible. On this route on ADA paved trails, we will stay on level pavement, accessible for wheelchairs and strollers. The path to Upper Falls is slightly uphill. Naturalist Mic has experience pushing wheelchairs and can assist. We take it slowly.      Along the way, visitors will learn how the waterfalls were formed and we will ponder why humans are drawn to powerful demonstrations of nature's strength.  The first overlook is about one block from the visitor center. There are overlo

events.title: New Deal at the Nature Store - CCC Program
events.description: It has been a rough couple years. Many of us have been out of work and in need of aid. Looking for a hand up, not a handout. Come learn about amazing new opportunities to get back to work and make a lasting difference. The passage of the Emergency Conservation Works Act in March of 1933 created thousands of new jobs. After a short presentation the CCC camp superintendent will take prospective enrollees around the grounds to look at examples of the work underway in the park.

events.title: Monarch Butterfly Hike
events.description: Monarchs are beginning to gather for their long flight to Mexico and sometimes flock to the park prairie. Look for some of these amazing pollinators on this guided tour.  We will meet at the park picnic shelter and then travel via car caravan over to the walk's starting point. Please come prepared with your own vehicle transportation. This program is possible through a partnership with MNDNR and Friends of Nerstrand Big Woods State Park.To learn more about the Friends of Nerstrand Big Woods State Park visit their website by  clicking here .  Trail Conditions: Choose from a 0.9 mile or 1.4 mile
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Build a Beaver Dam
events.description: Beavers are one of natures' greatest engineers! Join us to learn about these amazing critters and try your hand at building your own mini beaver dam! Meet at the Picnic Area at 3:00pm

events.title: Animal Detectives- Nature Table
events.description: Do you know your mammals? Can you match which skull and fur belongs to what animal? Help solve a nature mystery by examining teeth, skull shapes, and fur textures to deduce the identity of some fascinating Minnesotan critters. Drop by the naturalist table at the visitor center.

events.description: Calling all Junior Rangers! William O'Brien State Park is one of a few state parks that boarder the St. Croix National Scenic Riverway. Come learn about some plants and animals that make William O'Brien and the St. Croix Riverway such a unique places and have the opportunity to earn your state and national junior ranger badges. Meet at the amphitheater. All children must be accompanied by adults.

events.description: Ride in a 10-person canoe while learning about the history of the area, including ducks and geese that have been hunted in the area for centuries. Participants must be at least 10 years old.  Registration is required and limited to the first 18 people to sign up for each tour. Paddles and life jackets are provided.  To register, email erin.fallon@state.mn.us before 8 a.m. on Saturday, August 29. This program will be canceled if the windspeed is above 15mph, or if there is thunder or lightening. events.title: Creatures of the Potholes: Investigation Station
events.description: Tons of legs, jet propulsion, or a built-in snorkel!? Drop by to discover the strange adaptations of mysterious creatures that call the park's glacial potholes home. Most participants spend about ten minutes at this ongoing station. Find us outside the park's visitor center.

events.title: Don't Move a Mussel (best for ages 3 to adult)
events.description: The St. Croix River supports an astonishing diversity of native mussels. Hear the story of how some species became endangered. Touch shells of various shapes and discover how they trick fish into raising their babies.  Drop by the Visitor Center anytime during the program. Most people spend about 10 minutes at this station.

events.title: Mini Monsters
events.description: Join our naturalist to learn about the life in the river.  We will use nets and buckets to catch the critters the call the river home. We will see what they can tell us about the water quality of the Whitewater River.
events.address: Whitewater State Park - Visitor Center, MN

events.title: Bats: Echoes in the Night
events.description: Explore the fascinating world of Minnesota's bats! Uncover the secrets of their nocturnal navigation and discover which species call our state home. Join us in unraveling the mysteries of these often-misunderstood mammals! Meet at the amphitheater. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Prairie Palette: A colorful walk through the prairie
events.description: This time of year, the prairie starts to change its colors. Come walk through the prairie in search of a rainbow of colors! Meet at the Sunset Lake Trailhead.  The trail will be a mowed grass trail with relatively even terrain. There are two small hills on the trail that we will be walking up.  Please dress for the weather conditions that day. Feel free to bring binoculars to spot our feathered friends. This program will be cancelled if there are storms or poor air quality conditions.  While this program is free, there is an entrance fee for the park. A day permit is $7, or an annual permit is

events.title: National Toasted Marshmallow Day
events.description: Meet in amphitheater behind park office What happens in the park after the sun goes down? Join us around the campfire for an interactive exploration of the nighttime world. Use your senses to uncover hidden sounds, mysterious scents, fascinating textures, and surprising sights as we discover how both people and wildlife experience the dark. And for our sense of taste, we will be roasting marshmallows!

events.title: Buzzing With Excitement: Guided Wildflower Walk
events.description: Join Park Naturalist Mic on a slow walk around a loop at the Shipwreck Creek Campground, which has been seeded with native flowers found throughout the state of Minnesota. On this hike, less than a mile in length on flat ground, you will gain appreciation for how flowers are perfectly designed to interact with the world around them. Canceled if lightning.   Meet by Shipwreck Creek sanitation building. Mic will be by the picnic bench.
events.address: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park, MN

events.title: Orienteering Scavenger Hunt
events.description: Join us at the Trail Center for an introduction to orienteering, a sport where you use a compass to navigate between two points. We will walk through how to use a compass, and then practice those skills during an animal track scavenger hunt at the beach!
events.address: Bear Head Lake State Park, MN

events.title: Five Facts in Five Minutes: Manoomin (Wild Rice)
events.description: Near the Mississippi Headwaters (at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center if rain.)  Only have a minute to learn about Itasca State Park? Stop at the naturalist station and explore manoomin (wild rice) with Annette Drewes, manoomin (wild rice) researcher as you visit the Headwaters of the Mississippi River.

events.title: Kids' Activity: Fish Printing
events.description: Create beautiful Gyotaku art (fish print) from a soft fish replica!  Look for the Naturalist in the Beach Area, any time within the 2 hours. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.

events.description: The naturalist will be roving about the campground answering "What to do?" and "What did I just see?" questions, and handing out fun surprises for the kids. Watch for the naturalist walking the campground loops.

events.title: Fire Shelter Race!
events.description: A fire shelter is the last line of defense a wildland fire fighter has.  People working on prescribed fires carry them too incase of the worst case scenario: getting trapped by a fire.  How fast can you get inside a fire shelter? And how does such thin foil protect people from a fire? Stop by to discover more and even try deploying a shelter yourself. Meet at the St. Croix Lodge.

This tour is best for ages 6 and up. Meet outside the park's visitor center. This program takes place entirely outdoors and will be canceled or postponed in the event of lightning or thunder.

Discover how massive lava flows, glacial rivers and human interest in the area shaped the impressive landscape. Expect rocky terrain and short stairs on this 1/4-mile walk. This tour is best for ages 6 and up. Meet outside the park's visitor center. This program takes place entirely outdoors and will be canceled or postponed in the event of lightning or thunder.

events.title: Explore Potholes on a Guided Tour
events.description: These potholes aren't what you think! Explore GLACIAL potholes and unique geology on a walk with a park guide. Uncover stories hidden within scenic river views. Discover how massive lava flows, glacial rivers and human interest in the area shaped the impressive landscape. Expect rocky terrain and short stairs on this 1/4-mile walk. This tour is best for ages 6 and up. Meet outside the park's visitor center. This program takes place entirely outdoors and will be canceled or postponed in the event of lightning or thunder.

events.title: A Tale of Two Rivers
events.description: The Kettle and St. Croix rivers define the boundaries of St. Croix State Park, and their waters have played a significant role in the history of the land.  Come explore how water has shaped this place in recent and ancient memory. Meet at the Kettle River Overlook

events.title: Nature Cart: Animal Tracks and Signs
events.description: What animals were on the trails before you? Join the park naturalist to learn how to read the signs that wildlife leaves behind and the stories they tell. Investigate animal tracks and signs with hands on activities. Stop by anytime from 2:00pm-3:00pm To attend, meet by the picnic tables near the swim pond.

events.title: Itasca�s Historic Photo Scavenger Hunt
events.description: Meet at the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center. Follow in the footsteps of park visitors of the past as we recreate historic photos around Itaca State Park! Join us for a presentation of some of Itasca�s historic photos before going out and recreating your choice of historic photos on your own! Return to the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center by 3:30 p.m. to print one of your favorite photos and receive a prize!

events.title: Music Under the Pines: North Wind Clarinets
events.description: LIVE MUSIC at the Forest Inn!  This ultra-talented quintet plays a spirited arrangement of classic, jazz, swing, and contemporary tunes on a variety of clarinets, from the big bass to the tiny Eb. Players are Beth Hahn and Deane Johnson from Park Rapids, Peg Rickert and Sarah Sundeen from Bemidji, and Vicki Magnuson from Bagley.   This is an indoor event. Seating is provided. The Music Under the Pines summer concert series is sponsored in partnership with the Friends of Itasca State Park. The Friends will host an ice cream social at this event.

events.title: Skins and Skulls
events.description: All animals are uniquely adapted for their survival.  Learn about the adaptations of various animals that live in Minnesota by examining their skins and skulls. NO REGISTRATION NEEDED. Meet at Thomas C. Savage Visitor Center.

events.title: Mystery Tracks
events.description: The game is afoot at and leaving tracks at St. Croix State Park - can you figure out whodunnit?  Come investigate the tracks and other signs animals leave behind to see if you can decipher the clues and solve the mystery!

events.title: Prairie Patrol (all ages)
events.description: Prairies are very dynamic ecosystems that can change week to week depending on what is blooming. Splashes of yellows, purples, and pinks in the morning sun is enough to make you swoon. Come explore and identify wildflowers and learn why prairies are so important to protect. Meet at the visitor center.

events.title: Archery in the Park
events.description: Come participate in one of the oldest arts still practiced today.  Families and individuals alike can learn the valuable skill of archery free of charge. No experience is required and all equipment is provided. Stop by the beach house anytime during the program.  Children must be at least 8 years old to participate and must be accompanied by an adult.  No personal equipment is allowed. Meet at the Horse Camp. Children must be accompanied by an adult. Programs and events may be canceled due to inclement weather. A park vehicle pass is required to enter the park and can be purchased at the park

events.title: Owl Pellets
events.description: What is an owl's favorite food? Come find out by opening up an owl pellet and discover what they have been eating. We'll also learn what makes an owl an efficient predator. We'll be meeting in the classroom located in the downstairs area of the Interpretive Center - also known as the Trail Center.

events.title: Get Hooked on Fishing
events.description: Come learn the basics of fishing and what you can expect to catch in the lake.  The program is designed with beginners and ages 6-11 in mind, but all are welcome to participate. Minors must be accompanied by an adult. All equipment is provided.  This program is limited to 10 fishing participants. Please pre-register by contacting Savannah at: savannah.stephenson@state.mn.us Pre-registration ends at 3:00 p.m. on Saturday, August 29. We will be meeting at the fishing pier at the Beach.

events.title: Double Lives of Dragonflies: Investigation Station
events.description: What does a young dragonfly look like? When does it get wings? Discover the strange double lives of dragonflies at this ongoing, drop-in activity station. Find us at the visitor center. Most visitors spend about ten minutes exploring activities. Canceled in the event of rain.

events.title: Park Invaders Nature Cart
events.description: Many sneaky plants and animals are taking over our ecosystems! Stop by the picnic shelter to find out how to identify invasive species and what you can do to prevent their spread. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: From Flames to Flowers
events.description: You have likely heard about some of the devastating wildfires impacting communities around the nation and world. Did you know that sometimes fire is beneficial? We invite you to join our naturalist on a hike exploring the prairie and how we use fire to keep this ecosystem healthy.   Meet at the picnic shelter. Please bring your own transportation. After a brief introduction, we will hop into our vehicles to travel 4 miles to the start of the prairie trailhead. This hike consists of roughly one mile of mostly, flat mowed grass trail. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is requi
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Boreal Birding
events.description: Bring your binoculars for this relaxed paced walk as we search for colorful spring migrants and resident songbirds. Learn how to use tools to identify birds by sight and sound, and experience the wonderful summer season at Bear Head Lake State Park. Birders of all experience levels are welcome for this guided walk, and we will meet at the Trail Center. A few pairs of binoculars will be available.
events.address: Bear Head Lake State Park, MN

events.title: Seeing the CCC: Walking Tour
events.description: Meet outside Forest Inn, across from Douglas Lodge. Curious about the Civilian Conservation Corps? Want to be able to identify CCC buildings? How has the legacy of the CCC continued today? Join us on a walking tour starting at the Forest Inn and ending at the Old Timer�s Cabin! The tour will last an hour, and the Old Timer�s Cabin will be open for exploration for an hour following the tour.

events.title: Discovery Table - Rocks Talks
events.description: Rocks tell you a story about Earth's history if you know what to look for. Stop in anytime with your rocks to have the naturalist help you identify them and learn the stories of Jay Cooke State Park. Where to Meet? The table will be set up inside the River Inn Visitor Center. This program is ongoing, so stop in anytime.

events.title: Jr. Naturalist: Nature Walk
events.description: Meet outside Forest Inn (across from Douglas Lodge)    Kids, come explore the Itasca forest and search along the trail for things that belong and don't belong. This walk is around 1/2 mile round trip.

events.title: Woods and Wildflower Walk
events.description: Meet outside Douglas Lodge. Interested in the plants of Itasca State Park? Join us on a short walk to see what wildflowers are blooming along with the trees around them. We will be walking along the Dr. Roberts Trail, a trail noted for its variety of plants and bog boardwalk!

events.title: Mysteries in History: The Douglas Lodge Area
events.description: Meet in the Douglas Lodge Lobby. Once proclaimed a �jewel set in mud,� Douglas Lodge is a point of pride in Itasca State Park and is Itasca�s oldest surviving structure. Join us on a walking tour around Douglas Lodge and its surroundings to learn more about this �jewel� and how the park developed the �mud� surrounding it into a hotspot of activity.  Walk will be about one-third mile in length.

events.title: Bird Migration Walk (best for ages 8 to adult)
events.description: Whether you've never birded before or you can identify all Minnesota species by ear, this walk is for you! We'll share our observations and questions and use our group's knowledge to better understand the birds around us. Bring binoculars and a field guide if you have them, or borrow ours. This walk will cover up to a mile.  Meet at the Visitor Center at the start time. Leave an extra 10 minutes to drive to the visitor center parking lot and walk to the building.

events.title: Chasing Waterfalls Walking Tour
events.description: Join Park Naturalist on a tour of Gooseberry Falls State Park's four major waterfalls. We will see multiple views of Upper, Middle and Lower Falls on a route that covers about 2/3 of a mile on varying terrain, including many steps.  Along the way you will learn how the waterfalls were formed and will ponder why humans are drawn to powerful demonstrations of nature's strength. All ages welcome.  Meet outside the east side of the visitor center by program banner. Canceled if lightning.

events.title: Storytime in Nature- Hibernation!
events.description: Meet by the campfire circle outside the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds (in between Lake Itasca and the picnic shelter). Kids, do you like to read stories about nature and the outdoors? Join a naturalist volunteer as we enjoy reading stories outside. After the story, have fun making a craft together that you get to take home. NOTES: Adults must accompany children.

events.title: Peaceful Wildlife Hike
events.description: Join Park Naturalist on a peaceful, quiet hike to Lake Superior along the Gooseberry River. As we walk along the River View trail (approximately 1.75 mile round trip) we will use our senses to enjoy birds and other wildlife. During this time of day, we may see warblers foraging, bald eagles, waterfowl, deer, beaver, and otter in the river valley.  This path is packed gravel and clay. The majority of the trail is flat but there are some steeper slopes towards the lake. You may borrow a pair of binoculars for this hike.  Meet inside the visitor center West doors, near the wayside rest bathrooms.

events.title: Artist's Reception - MaryAnn Cleary
events.description: Tettegouche State Park hosts monthly art shows at the Visitor Center and our September artist is MaryAnn Cleary. Please join us for a reception with the artist.

events.title: What Happened to the Trees? (Emerald Ash Borer)- Nature Table
events.description: As you visit the park you might notice some tree trunks turning blonde. What is happening to the trees? Underneath the bark a sinister beetle is lurking, the Emerald Ash Borer. Do you have an Ash tree on your property? Come learn how to identify an infested Ash and how park staff are working to save its unique woodlands. Drop the naturalist table at the visitor center.

events.title: Nature Discovery Table: Nature is Yucky!
events.description: Meet in the Visitor Center.  Come on down to discover all kinds of cool things about nature! Animal skulls, feathers, furs, rocks or bugs, oh my! Each week there will be a different theme to engage your senses and explore the natural world up close. This time, learn about some icky, but fascinating things in nature! Stop by any time between 2:30 p.m. and 3:30 p.m. Meet in the Visitor Center.

events.title: Nature Game Night
events.description: Come one, come all, and join us for Nature Game Night!  Board games, cards, and puzzles for you to play and discover more about the people, plants, and animals that call St. Croix home.  There is something for everyone, so stop by the St. Croix Lodge and play a few rounds!

events.title: Morning Nature Hike
events.description: Meet outside the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center.  Enjoy the health benefits of nature on this morning walk. Lots of changes are happening with plants and animals as we transition from late summer to early fall. Walk distance is around one and a half miles and is on a paved trail.

events.title: Gitchi Gummi Trail Guided Hike
events.description: Enjoy a 1.5 mile guided hike with stunning views of Lake Superior. Learn about the young forest and enjoy the beginning of fall colors.  This hike is moderate in difficulty, come prepared with water to stay hydrated and hiking shoes.  Free parking in the wayside rest parking lot.

events.title: Bad Rap Bats
events.description: Vampires. Blood suckers. Creatures of the night. Bats have gotten a bad rap over hundreds of years. Stories have been told and retold that bats are something to be feared, but in reality, they do so much more good for humans than you think. Come and learn why bats shouldn't be feared and enjoy a bat bedtime story. Meet in the visitor center.

events.title: Nature Journaling and Flashlight Nature Walk
events.description: Meet in the Visitor Center.  Learn about the upcoming fall equinox and what is changing in the night sky, make a nature journal to take home and go for a nighttime nature walk using flashlights. Bring a flashlight to explore the park after sunset. Meet in the Visitor Center.

events.title: Here Fishy Fishy!
events.description: Did you know there are 162 species of fish that live in Minnesota?  St. Croix State Park has many kinds of fish in its waters, from minnows and chubs to bass, sturgeon, burbot, and trout.  Whether you are going fishing or merely curious about the shadows swimming around your legs as you wade, come take a peek underwater and discover a whole new world!

events.title: Fishing 101
events.description: Let's go fishing! Join us as we learn all about fishing - identifying species, casting, and more.  We provide the poles, bait and instructors. Minnesota residents do not need a fishing license for this activity.  Meet at the Public Boat Access Parking Lot. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.

events.title: Nature Table and Kids' Activity: Birds of a Feather
events.description: Come visit with a naturalist intern to explore why birds have different feathers and coloration, and how it benefits them in the wild. Then be the first to try our NEW kids' scavenger hunt, to test your birding skills and win a prize!  Look for the Naturalist across the parking lot from the Interpretive/Visitor Center, any time within the 2 hours. The building is closed due to construction. All programs will take place outdoors. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Nature Table and Kids' Activity: Birds of a Feather
events.description: Come visit with a naturalist intern to explore why birds have different feathers and coloration, and how it benefits them in the wild. Then be the first to try our NEW kids' scavenger hunt, to test your birding skills and win a prize!  Look for the Naturalist in the beach area, any time within the 2 hours. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.

events.title: Jr. Naturalist: Lookin at Leaves
events.description: Meet at the campfire circle by the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds.  Kids, learn about trees and their leaves from why trees have leaves and what leaves belong to which trees. Create leaf art to take home!

events.title: Bog Discovery: Bog Boardwalk Trivia
events.description: Meet at the Bog Boardwalk.  Take a stroll along one of the park's favorite trails and try to answer fun trivia questions about bogs along your way! The naturalist will also be at the end of the boardwalk if you want to learn more about bogs or nature in general. This is a self-guided program. The gravel Bog Walk Trail is one-mile one-way, a two-mile total trip there and back. The trailhead starts at the northwest end of the Aspen Lane parking lot and you will cross over HWY 20 and go to the right. Wear sturdy shoes for walking and bring water and a snack.

events.title: Fishing for Fun!
events.description: Let's have fun fishing at the park! This program is perfect for beginners ages 6-12. Learn how to cast, about what kinds of fish are in Lake Bemidji, the kinds of bait people use and try fishing off our fishing pier. Registration is required and is limited to 12 participants. To register, call the park office at 218-308-2300 or email christa.drake@state.mn.us. Fishing rods and bait will be provided. Children must be accompanied by an adult.  Minnesota residents do not need a fishing license, but all non-residents will need one.

events.title: Glow Hike Event
events.description: Ready to explore the park in a new light? Join us at Flandrau State Park for our Glow Hike event! This is a fun, family friendly night adventure on the trails. There will be self-guided hikes starting at 7:30, naturalist led activities about nocturnal creatures and more! The trail is a one-mile loop that is flat and suitable for people of all ages. Because the path is not paved, please wear sturdy and comfortable shoes. To be as bright as the moon, we recommend bringing glow sticks, wearing glow-in-the-dark paint or a bringing a flashlight!  Please meet at the Beach House to join the fun. A va

events.title: How to Recognize Different Types of Trees from Quite a Long Way Away and Up Close
events.description: Aspen, oak, pine... St. Croix State Park is home to many different species of both conifers and deciduous trees.  But there is more to trees than their leaves (or needles)!  Have you ever wondered how long trees live?  Did you know jack pine require fire to spread their seeds?  Just how many different kinds of oaks are there?  Come meet some of these giant organisms and get to the root of your curiosity! Meet at the St. Croix Lodge.

events.title: Nature Cart-Mammal Mania
events.description: What furry creatures can you discover? Join the park naturalist to learn how to identify Minneopa's mammals by investigating furs, bones and tracks. If interested, stop by the waterfall pavilion anytime from 3:00-4:00pm. Activities usually last 10-15 minutes.

events.title: Restoring Historic Landscapes (Oak Savanna)- Nature Table
events.description: Rolling Hills Savanna Trail has been a focal point for the past two winters with intensive restoration projects. Partnering with the Audubon Society, approximately 60 acres comprising the trail is in the beginning stages of its journey back to historic oak savanna. Check out some before photos of the project and go out and experience the trail yourself. Drop by the naturalist table at the visitor center.

events.title: The Peregrine Story A Conservation Comeback
events.description: For more than 45 years, researchers in Minnesota have been unraveling the mysteries of peregrine falcons, how they live, how they migrate, and how dedicated conservation efforts helped pull the species back from the brink. Our presenter, Jackie Fallon, is a wildlife biologist, master falconer, and educator with nearly four decades of experience. As the VP of Field Operations for the Midwest Peregrine Society and Minnesota�s state coordinator for peregrine monitoring, Jackie oversees research at more than 50 peregrine territories across Minnesota and Wisconsin. Jackie will be bringing a live pe
events.address: Forestville Mystery Cave State Park, MN

events.title: Talk with a Naturalist: Bat Chat
events.description: Swing by the Naturalist table at the Visitor Center to learn a little about Minnesota's Bats. What kinds of bats do we have? Where do they live? How do they benefit us? What challenges to they face?  How do I build a successful bat box?  Drop in and talk to park naturalist Jeremy to find the answers to all your bat related questions.
events.address: Whitewater State Park - Visitor Center, MN

events.title: Whitewater's POW Camp
events.description: Did you know that Whitewater State Park was once home to German Prisoners of War?  Come learn about one of lesser-known parts of Minnesota's history. What did they do here? Where did they go? What was life like being a prisoner? Did they cause mischief? Come find out!!
events.address: Whitewater State Park - Visitor Center, MN

events.title: Beavers in the Valley
events.description: Come learn all about nature's architects. We will learn about the adaptations that allow these amazing mammals to thrive in the Whitewater Valley. During the program we will also take a short walk and look at the construction project currently underway.
events.address: Whitewater State Park - South Picnic Area, MN

events.title: Junior Ranger: Miniature Worlds Magnified
events.description: An incredible, tiny world is hidden amongst the park's rocks and logs. Join the naturalist to explore the amazing world of lichens with microscopes, magnifying glasses and a short scavenger hunt. Expect to walk a quarter mile on mostly flat trails and grassy areas. Meet at the Campground Clubhouse building, next to the restrooms in the park's campground. Children must be accompanied by an adult.

events.title: Nature Station: Fungus Among Us (best for ages 3-adult)
events.description: Have you ever walked in the woods a few days after a good rain? Mushrooms are popping up everywhere, but they're only the tip of the iceberg. Join mushroom enthusiasts to discover what's happening below the surface. We'll explore the parts of a fungus under the park's projection microscope, and look at a variety of saprophytic friends.    Drop by the visitor center anytime during the program. Most visitors spend 10 minutes at this station.

events.title: Monarch Tagging
events.description: Did you know the Monarch Butterfly is our official state butterfly? This time of year, they are starting their incredible journey to wintering grounds in Mexico. Join us as we carefully catch and tag these amazing insects to help scientists learn more about them. In the event of rain this program will be canceled.  Long pants, closed toed shoes, and your favorite refillable water bottle are recommended for this activity. Program will mainly take place along a 1/4 mile stretch of flat mowed grass trail, but may require you to enter tall grass with uneven terrain. The program will meet at the pa
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Nature Storytime
events.description: Come experience the natural world through a nature themed story and activity! This program is designed for those ages 5-8, but all ages are welcome to participate. Children must be accompanied by a responsible adult. Meet at the amphitheater. The program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12 month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Owl about Owls
events.description: Haunting calls and silent flight make owls both mysterious and fascinating. Discover which owls live here as we explore what makes them successful creatures of the night. Meet at the amphitheater. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Majestic Mussels
events.description: Discover the hidden world beneath the St. Croix River! Come drop by and explore a nature table about the fascinating freshwater mussels of Minnesota. With over 50 native species, these incredible animals help keep our rivers clean. Visitors can examine real shells, play a mussel matching game, and uncover the amazing life cycle of mussels, including their remarkable partnership with fish. Suitable for all ages. Stop by at Duluth Junction, where the Gateway and Brown's Creek State Trails meet between 1 and 3 p.m.
events.address: Duluth Junction, Gateway State Trail, MN

events.title: Nature Story Time
events.description: Join a naturalist where we will read a story and learn about the natural world. The book for this program will be "The Prairie That Nature Built"; by Marybeth Lorbiecki. We will explore the prairie ecosystem and investigate the animals and plants that call it home.  This program is most suitable for children 10 and under.

events.title: Where will frogs go?: Investigation Station
events.description: Fall will be here soon and local frogs will start looking for their perfect place to overwinter. Where they go will depend on what type of frog they are. Join the park naturalist to discover how to tell Minnesota's frogs apart and discover the strange ways they spend the winter. This drop-in activity can be found in front of the visitor center. Most visitors spend about ten minutes at this station. Canceled in the event of rain.

events.title: Sand Point Bird Walk
events.description: Walk through the riparian forest and along the beach to Sand Point. Hope to see fall migrating warblers as well as resident birds of the forest, waterfowl, terns, gulls, and shorebirds. Bring binoculars. The trail is well maintained and flat. The full loop is approximately 2 miles long. When birding, this can take 2-4 hours depending upon how many birds we're seeing, but you can leave whenever you would like. No need to register but if you have any questions, email janetmalotky@gmail.com.  Meet at the Sand Point parking lot off of US 61.

events.title: Night Walk
events.description: Meet outside the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center. Walk along the trail and explore your senses and the senses of animals that are normally awake while we are sleeping. This walk is around 1/2 mile long. Flashlights are welcome, but we will keep them off till the end of the walk.

events.title: Discover the Life Beneath Your Feet
events.description: There is a whole world hidden beneath your feet! Join the park naturalist as we uncover the secret lives of Minnesota's underground animals. Discover the amazing adaptations that help them dig, find food, and survive in the dark. Then put your own skills to the test with a hands-on challenge using the knowledge you've gained. This program is for all ages. Join the fun at the stone shelter in the park's southern picnic area. Children must be accompanied by an adult.

events.title: Summer Concert: Donna and Greg Gaston
events.description: Meet at the Amphitheater.  The Friends of Lake Bemidji State Park and the North Country Snowmobile Club present our annual Music Under the Pines summer concert series.  Come out to enjoy acoustic folk rock music by Donna and Greg Gaston. Concerts are held at our outdoor amphitheater under the tall pine trees. If it is raining, it will be held inside the Visitor Center.

events.title: Nature Play for Kids - Seeds! (best for ages 4-11)
events.description: The Nature Play Area is a magical space, shaded by red pine trees. A naturalist will lead activities around a nature theme. This week we'll explore a variety of seeds!    Find us near the E Lane of the Main Campground. There is a small parking lot and the Nature Play Area is a 30 second walk from there.  Best for ages 4-11, but all ages welcome. Seating is available. Kids, bring an adult with you. Try to make it by the start time so you don't miss the fun!

events.title: Volunteer: Collect Prairie Seeds! (all ages welcome)
events.description: All ages are welcome - great for kids and adults.   What to Expect  The Prairie Care program is working to diversify 500 acres of prairie at Wild River. We collect seeds from about 80 species of prairie plants each year and make seed mixes to spread after prescribed burns. Join us for a couple hours of seed collection. No experience is necessary. We will be walking off-trail into some beautiful prairie areas. Depending on the time of year we may see harmless snakes. If you enjoy this work, you may decide to become a Species Steward and "adopt" one or more species to monitor and collect on you

events.title: Volunteer: Collect Prairie Seeds! (all ages welcome)
events.description: All ages are welcome - great for kids and adults.   What to Expect  The Prairie Care program is working to diversify 500 acres of prairie at Wild River. We collect seeds from about 80 species of prairie plants each year and make seed mixes to spread after prescribed burns. Join us for a couple hours of seed collection. No experience is necessary. We will be walking off-trail into some beautiful prairie areas. Depending on the time of year we may see harmless snakes. If you enjoy this work, you may decide to become a Species Steward and "adopt" one or more species to monitor and collect on you

events.title: Annual Labor Day Weekend Friends of Lake Bemidji State Park Pancake Breakfast
events.description: Meet at the Dining Hall.  Indulge in a morning of delicious generosity at our Pancake Breakfast! Join us for a stack of fluffy pancakes, tasty sausage, hot coffee and refreshing juice served with a side of community spirit. Bring your appetite and your support as we flip for a cause. Your participation will help us make every bite a step towards positive change for the park. Stop by any time between 8 a.m. and 10 a.m. at the Dining Hall. Help save the environment by bringing your own plates and utensils.

events.title: Live Peregrine Falcon Meet & Greet
events.description: Drop into the Whitewater Valley Visitor Center to get up close with a live peregrine falcon! Jackie Fallon of the Midwest Peregrine Society will be on hand to answer questions and share about the remarkable recovery of these impressive birds of prey.
events.address: Whitewater State Park- Visitor Center, MN

events.title: Family Fun! Bingo Scavenger Hunt
events.description: Meet at the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center. Are you ready to take a closer look at the plants, animals, and features of Itasca State Park? Pick up a bingo card at the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center. Set off to explore the park while looking for animals and their signs, characteristics of plants, historic sites, and geological features. Once you have checked off enough of the scavenger hunt items to achieve a bingo, bring the completed card to the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center and claim your prize!

events.title: Nature Stories: One North Star
events.description: Meet in the Visitor Center.  Welcome to our enchanting nature story time, a magical experience crafted for curious minds of any age! Immerse your little ones in the wonders of the natural world through a delightful blend of stories, crafts and other fun activities that will spark their imaginations and ignite a love for learning. Afterwards, you can spend time in the Visitor Center and play puppets or a fishing game, do a puzzle, color, play dress-up or get to see and touch soft animal furs! Adults must accompany children.
events.address: Big Bog State Recreation Area, MN

events.title: Wings and Things: Investigation Station
events.description: If you could have wings, would you want them to be feathery, leathery, or full of colorful scales? Many creatures have wings, but their designs vary quite a bit. Join the naturalist to investigate a few of these designs and learn the benefits and challenges of each at this drop-in station. Most visitors spend 10 minutes at this ongoing activity. Canceled in the event of rain.

events.title: Hidden Underwater World
events.description: Meet at the Beach.  Did you know there are tiny things that live and grow in the water? Come on down to the beach to see these things up close using a microscope and magnifying glasses. What will we discover? Meet at the Beach at the Southern Unit.
events.address: Big Bog State Recreation Area, MN

events.title: Falcons Live!
events.description: The peregrine falcon has long fascinated people across the globe, known for its dramatic migration and amazing flight. Where 60 years ago there were none, today nearly 350 nesting pairs of falcons make their home in the Upper Midwest. Jackie Fallon, with the Midwest Peregrine Society, will present this program with several live birds to help us understand the past, present, and future of peregrine falcons in Frontenac State Park, Minnesota, and the Upper Midwest. Make sure to bring your camera for a great opportunity to see these amazing birds. The event will take place right next to the Range

events.title: Navigating by the Stars
events.description: All around the world people look up at the night sky and see the stars.  For centuries (even after the invention of GPS) people have used the stars to find their way, and you can too!  Join us to discover the secrets of celestial navigation. If the weather is clear bring a blanket to lie upon while you stargaze.  Bug spray recommended. Meet at the St. Croix Lodge.  After an introduction, we will car caravan to our stargazing site.

events.title: Navigating by the Stars
events.description: All around the world people look up at the night sky and see the stars.  For centuries (even after the invention of GPS) people have used the stars to find their way, and you can too!  Join us to discover the secrets of celestial navigation. If the weather is clear bring a blanket to lie upon while you stargaze.  Bug spray recommended. Meet at the St. Croix Lodge.  After an introduction, we will car caravan to our stargazing site.

events.title: Dragonflies- Master Hunters (all ages)
events.description: Dragonflies are one of the most successful predators on the planet boasting a hunting success rate of 95%! What about their bodies makes them such extraordinary hunters? Get an opportunity to observe dragonflies up close and make and take your very own dragonfly home with you. Meet at the visitor center.

events.title: Migrate, Hibernate, or Adapt (all ages)
events.description: The fall months are here. With shorter days and cooler mornings plants and animals are starting to prepare for the winter ahead. How do animals cope with long winters? Animals migrate, hibernate, or adapt. Find out what animals do in the winter with a fun matching game and see what happens to an animal's body while it hibernates with an energy conservation science experiment.  Meet in the visitor center.

events.title: Camo Creatures Treasure Hunt
events.description: Many creatures living in St. Croix State Park make use of camouflage.  Discover some of these creatures and challenge your observational skills spotting objects in a camouflage treasure hunt!  Stop by the Trail Center Parking Lot (Gate 2) to join the hunt!

events.title: Fossil Field Trip
events.description: During this program we will go and look for ancient sea life that lived in the area hundreds of millions of years ago. We'll start with a brief introduction at the visitor center, then drive out of the park 9 miles to hunt for fossils.    Bring transportation.
events.address: Whitewater State Park - Visitor Center, MN

events.title: Secrets of Skulls: Investigation Station
events.description: Skulls reveal incredible secrets about the animals they belong to... if you know what to look for. Take a close look at several replica skulls from Minnesota mammals and learn to read their clues with a park naturalist. What will you discover? Most participants spend about ten minutes at this drop-in activity station. Find us near the visitor center. Canceled in the event of rain.

events.title: A.L.P.s at Whitewater - Improving Habitat for Insects
events.description: Join us for our monthly A.L.P.'s at Whitewater program (Advanced Learning Program) hosted by the Friends of Whitewater State Park! This month we welcome Jessica Miller. Jessica will teach us how collapsing insect populations worldwide threaten everything from wild birds to the food on our plate. But it's not too late to turn things around! Once habitat is restored, insects repopulate quickly. Even small patches are critical places for food, reproduction, and over wintering habitat. Join us to learn how to create �insect friendly� spaces for the unsung heroes of our environment.

events.title: In Seine for fishes
events.description: What is a fish or a seine? Why does Minnesota have limitations on how many fish of certain species you can keep? We will answer these questions and more during this seining program.  If you would like to know what species of fish inhabit the water of the Mississippi and Minnesota Rivers at Fort Snelling State Park, then come join us.  The Naturalists will use a large net to scoop up fish from the river and identify them. NO REGISTRATION NEEDED. Due to water level fluctuation, location will be determined on day of program, please follow posted sign once in the park.

events.title: Wellness by Water: Yoga by the Lake
events.description: Meet in the picnic grounds by the Lakeside Museum. Relax and unwind with Yoga by the Lake, catered to all ages and levels of physical fitness! Enjoy nature while benefitting from yoga as the calming view of Lake Itasca and the towering pines overhead center you.  Notes: Participants should bring a mat, blanket, or beach towel and should wear comfortable clothing. Led by personal yoga trainers. All levels welcome.

events.title: Getting Ready Fall Nature Hike
events.description: Fall is a busy time for the plants and animals of the Big Woods. Join our park naturalist on a hike to find out the many ways that they get ready for the coming winter. Hike covers roughly a mile and includes steps, a portion of boardwalk and hilly terrain. Sturdy shoes are recommended. Front and backpack carriers are encouraged for younger children as the trail is not stroller friendly. Meet inside the park office building. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Nature Storytime: Bats
events.description: Come experience the natural world through a nature themed story and activity! This program is designed for those ages 5-8, but all ages are welcome to participate. Children must be accompanied by a responsible adult. Meet in the park office. The program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12 month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Intro to Mothing
events.description: Join Minnesota Biological Survey moth and butterfly specialist Kyle Johnson to explore the world of moths. This program will start in the picnic shelter at 8:00 p.m. with an informative presentation about these magnificent insects. Then we will head outside to experience moth surveying in action. Be prepared for light walking to and from the survey stations. All ages are welcome to attend; children must be accompanied by an adult. Please note: the main program will conclude at 11:00 p.m.; however, participants are welcome to stay later as surveys will continue overnight. *Event is scheduled fo

events.title: SPECIAL PROGRAM: Women in Conservation
events.description: Girl Scouts Love State Parks Weekend - Scouts are encouraged to attend this program. However, everyone is welcome! Learn from various Mille Lacs Kathio and Father Hennepin State Park female staff about why and how they chose a career with the Minnesota DNR. Brief stories from an Operations Supervisor, PAT Associate, NR Specialist and Naturalist will be followed by a Q&A session. The last part will allow Girl Scouts (and others) to ask the panel question about their career, as well as their passion for the outdoors and conservation.   Meet inside the Trail Center, located beside the horse camp.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park Trivia
events.description: Spend some time exploring and learning about Kathio, then challenge yourself to a fun game of park trivia. People can play individually or in a small group. However, only on exclusive Kathio leather patch will be given away to the winning person/group. All ages welcome! Meet at the amphitheater, located next to the Interpretive/Visitor Center. The building is closed due to construction. All programs will take place outdoors. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Fossil Fast Facts
events.description: This fun nature table will explore Minnesota's fossil world and teach you about some of the common fossils found here.  Drop by and learn some fun fossil facts!

events.title: Owl Prowl
events.description: We often hear them calling in the dark of night, but most of us are unfamiliar with the elusive creatures known as owls.  At this program, you will learn how to identify the owls of Afton State Park by their calls and appearance.  After the presentation, we�ll call the owls. This program is guaranteed to be a "hoot" for all ages! Meet at the Visitor Center and come prepared to step outside for a short while after the presentation, you may need a light.

events.title: Whitewater WMA - Autumn Adventure
events.description: Join us for a journey down that old country road. We'll be taking a relaxing autumn hike while looking for hints of the past. This 2.6 mile hike will take us into the Whitewater WMA, a large swath of public land just down the road from the park. This often-unexplored area provides opportunities for years of new discoveries and adventures.   Distance 2.6 Miles  Reservations are required.  Email jeremy.darst@state.mn.us or call 507-312-2301.
events.address: Meet at Carley State Park Flagpole, MN

events.title: Owl Be There
events.description: Owls have long made this park home. Bring your keen eyesight as we walk and talk about these stealthy hunters.  No registration required. Meet at the Thomas C. Savage Visitor Center (two miles from park entrance. Plan for an additional 10 minute drive through the park).

events.title: Storytime at Minneopa
events.description: Curious about nature? Join the park naturalist for a nature themed story and a craft! Activities are geared towards kids ages 3-5 but all ages are welcome. Children must be accompanied by a responsible adult. Meet by the Waterfall Pavillion The program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12 month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.

events.title: Migrating Birds Walk
events.description: What birds are getting ready for fall migration? Join the park naturalist to go bird watching on a short, flat 1 mile walk through woods and prairie.  Meet at the Group Camp Picnic area at 10:30am

events.title: A walk in the park
events.description: Fort Snelling State Park is situated right in the middle of a large metropolitan area with busy highways, railroads, river systems, and an International Airport.  It is one of the most visited state parks in Minnesota by hikers, bikers, skiers, and motorists.  Despite high human recreation, wildlife thrives with ease.  Come join the naturalist for a walk to see if we could spot any urban wildlife. NO REGISTRATION NEEDED. Meet at Thomas C. Savage Visitor Center.

events.title: Red Jacket Valley Park Canoe Adventure
events.description: Embark on an exciting family adventure with a beginner canoe program with Minnesota State Park staff! This adventure will go over the basics of canoeing while enjoying the beauty of Red Valley Jacket Lake. Participants must be 8 years of age or older and children 15 years of age or under must be accompanied by an adult.  To join, registration is   REQUIRED  , please email   augusta.grumdahl@state.mn.us  . Once registration is confirmed, additional information and details will be emailed before the day of the program.

events.title: How to survive and find way home
events.description: The thought of taking a short walk through the wilderness and suddenly not knowing where you are, can be a little nerve wrecking.    Fortunately, with some knowledge and practice you can put these worries to rest.  Find your way to Fort Snelling State Park and learn some basic survival skills.  Meet at the Thomas C. Savage Visitor Center  NO REGISTRATION NEEDED

events.title: Camping at Kathio... 3,500 Years Ago
events.description: Step back in time as we visit locations where archaeologists found evidence of a village from the 1600s and a �“campsite�” from over 3,000 years ago.  Meet in front of the Interpretive/Visitor Center. The building is closed due to construction. All programs will take place outdoors. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Itasca's Mysteries in History: The Itasca Biological Station
events.description: Meet at Tester's Hub located at the Itasca Biological Station (along Main Park Drive, watch for signs). This program has been canceled.  In 1907, the University of Minnesota began its first field classes in Itasca State Park, a tradition that continues today at the Itasca Biological Station and Laboratories. On this tour, you'll uncover the rich history of this iconic site while learning about cutting-edge biological education and research that takes place here.  Visit the Biome Center, a modern hub for current field classes, before stepping back in time to the site of the historic State Park

events.title: A Walk to Our Grandmother Cedars
events.description: Take a slow-paced walk to a magnificent grove of old-growth Northern White Cedars that have survived the logging era and likely even longer. These Grandmother Cedars are estimated to be 200 - 400 years old.  Take a 1.3-mile hike along the Zhaaboominikaani-ziibi (Gooseberry River) and listen to stories of these novel and elegant trees.  Meet outside the visitor center East doors by the banner.  Cancelled if lightning.  Free parking is available at the Wayside Rest parking lot (main visitor lot).

events.title: Music by Aimee Nordlund
events.description: Aimee Nordlund, who is a musician from Fergus Falls, MN. She is a piano teacher, choir director, pianist and vocalist.  Aimee performs a wide variety of music, from folk to gospel, from Johnny Cash to Judy Garland. She loves a sing-along and believes that music is better together!

events.title: Fungi Walk with Master Naturalist
events.description: Volunteer Master Naturalist Pam Miller will lead a walk to talk about fungi that grow in the park in the fall and their relationship to trees. Fall edible mushrooms include maitake (hen of the woods). We'll hope to find some! Wear closed shoes and socks, long pants and long sleeves, and bring tick and mosquito protection. Questions? Email pamelamarianmiller@gmail.com. Meet at the campground shower building kiosk. This event is free. Vehicles need to display a valid MN State Park Permit upon entering park. Please stop by the office or purchase beforehand. $7 one-day permit, $35 year-round permi

events.title: Shaping the St. Croix Valley- Geology Walk
events.description: The St. Croix Valley didn't form overnight. It took millions of years of fault lines, ancient oceans, and glaciers to shape the valley. How do we know this? The story is written in our rocks. In this program we will explore geologic events, landforms, and rock types, while taking in views of the modern-day St. Croix Valley. A 1.6-mile walk on the Riverside Trail will be included in the program. The trail used is flat with crushed gravel. Meet at Shelter 1 in the day use area.

events.title: Busy, Busy Beavers Walk (all ages)
events.description: Do you have what it takes to be a beaver? Can you drag branches with your teeth and swim in icy water and barely feel a thing? Come learn about adaptations that help beavers survive in their wetland habitat and how beavers engineer whole ecosystems. A 1.5-mile hike will be included in the program around the Beaver Lodge Trail. This trail is flat and a combination of asphalt and mowed grass. Meet at the visitor center.

events.title: Old Timer�s Cabin and the Civilian Conservation Corps
events.description: Held at the Old Timer�s Cabin, located along the boardwalk of Dr. Roberts Trail, below Douglas Lodge  Only 4 (massive) logs tall, learn more about this Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) constructed building as well as what life was like in the CCC. Feel free to stop by at your leisure and visit with the naturalist volunteer.

events.title: Phenology of Afton
events.description: Phenology is the study of the timings in the natural world, and fall is full of fun events occurring!  Visit the visitor center for a short program followed by a stroll where we will explore what is happening in Afton now.

events.title: Geocaching
events.description: Join us for a real-life treasure hunt as you learn the basics of geocaching using GPS technology. This beginner-friendly program will introduce you to how GPS units work and guide you on a search for hidden caches in the park. A limited number of GPS units will be available to borrow, or feel free to bring your own.

events.title: Exploration Station: Great Northern Diver: Tackling Threats to the Common Loon
events.description: Take a dive- deep into the underwater world of the Common Loon. At this exciting Exploration Station outside of the visitor center, you will learn how these birds are designed to dive deep and what threats they face in our lakes. Learn how to tackle these threats today!

events.title: Sewing Nature Pillowcases
events.description: Meet at the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center. Interested in learning how to sew? Come and learn the basics of sewing here at Itasca State Park! Sew a nature-themed pillowcase to take on your camping adventures! Pillowcase fabric will feature plants and animals found in Itasca! All experience levels are welcome! Supplies, materials, and sewing machines will be provided (feel free to bring your own sewing machine). Suitable for ages 10 and over.  Space is limited. Email to register at Anna.Fairbanks@state.mn.us. Email by 8 a.m. on Saturday, September 19 to register.

events.title: Wanted: Invasive Species
events.description: There�s a new �most wanted� list in the park and it�s filled with invasive species! Stop by the Visitor Center amphitheater anytime from 10-11:30am and learn how to identify these species during a fun activity, how they impact our ecosystem and what you can do to help!

events.title: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park Scavenger Hunt
events.description: Grab a Scavenger Hunt Form at the Park Office to start your adventure!
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Who- Cooks- For -You? Owl Pellet Dissection (all ages)
events.description: What does an owl make for lunch? Come find out firsthand by dissecting owl pellets and find out how they are such amazing nighttime hunters. Meet in the visitor center.

events.title: Dragonfly Friends- Nature Table
events.description: Dragonflies love to munch on mosquitoes and flies that bother us during our hikes. What makes them great hunters? Learn about their bodies while making your very own dragonfly friend that will protect you on your next hike. Drop by the naturalist table at the visitor center.

events.title: Birding Basics
events.description: Ever want to try out birding? Come to the Visitor Center where we will go over techniques, tips, and technologies that can be used for birders of all ages and abilities!  This program is for new birders and will have a short presentation followed by an excursion outside to bird!

events.title: SPECIAL EVENT: Archaeology Day
events.description: Come enjoy a day full of demonstrations, displays and activities that highlight the archaeology and rich cultural heritage of the Mille Lacs area.   Co-sponsored by MNDNR, MAS, and SCSU. The event will take place in the park�s picnic area, located in front of the Interpretive/Visitor Center and near the swimming hole. The building is closed due to construction. All activities will take place outdoors. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the event.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Brilliant Bears
events.description: Bears are amazing creatures that live closer than most would think!  Visit this nature table to take a sneak peek into their amazing world near the Stillwater trail head of the Brown's Creek State Trail
events.address: Brown's Creek State Trail Stillwater, MN

events.title: Where the Waters Meet
events.description: For thousands of years people have followed the rivers to where the park is located today. During this trail walk, visit the sites where the past and present meet and gain a better understanding of why this area is so significant.  No registration required. Meet at the Thomas C. Savage Visitor Center (two miles from park entrance. Plan for an additional 10 minute drive through the park). This walk will be just under a mile on flat, paved and gravel trails.

events.title: Minnesota Mussels
events.description: What do Monkeyfaces, Heelsplitters, and Pocketbooks have in common? They are just a few species of mussels that call Minnesota's waters home! Mussels play an important role in the health of our state's freshwater ecology, but most species are threatened or endangered. Stop by just outside the visitor center any time between 1:00-2:00PM to learn more about these freshwater friends.

events.title: Brilliant Beavers: Investigation Station
events.description: A beaver's unique adaptations help them change the landscape in surprising ways. Drop by to discover how they do their work and where you can find evidence of them at the park. Find this ongoing station outside the park's visitor center. Most participants spend about ten minutes. Canceled in the event of rain.

events.title: Animal Tracks
events.description: Many animals live in the park, but we might not always know they are there. Use your investigative skills to examine some of the clues they leave behind to let us know who they are. Meet at the picnic shelter. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Fall Color Hike
events.description: Reds, oranges, and yellows transform the Big Woods into a landscape full of beauty in the fall.  Join our naturalist for a hike exploring this season of change. Hike covers roughly a mile and includes steps, a portion of boardwalk and hilly terrain. Sturdy shoes are recommended. Front and backpack carriers are encouraged for younger children as the trail is not stroller friendly. Meet at the picnic shelter. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online o
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Celebrate The Salmon Run
events.description: Celebrate the Pink Salmon spawning run up the Gooseberry River! This unique salmon run happens in the fall when non-native Pacific Pink Salmon migrate from Lake Superior up the Gooseberry River to the Lower Falls pool, where they spawn and die. Talk to naturalists about this phenomenon and make a fish print while supplies last. The exact dates of the salmon run are unknown, but this is the predicted time based on past migrations.   Find the salmon run and naturalists below Lower Falls. Park for free at the wayside rest and walk .2 miles to Lower Falls.

events.title: Fall Color Extravaganza
events.description: Every year the changing colors of the forest herald the approach of autumn.  Did you know that many of the colors we see in leaves are caused by chemicals present in the leaf all year round?  Why do we see different colors at different times of the year?  How do we see color at all?  Drop by to explore these and other fall color questions and try your hand at some fall nature art! Drop in at the Lake Clayton Picnic Shelter

events.title: Fall Leaf Color Walk
events.description: Bring your young ones to Lake Bemidji State Park to experience the colorful season of fall! As we go on a leisurely walk, we will learn why leaves change color and explore how many colors we can find in the forest. Meet by the Playground. We will be walking along the paved Rocky Point Trail up to the overlook and back, which is about 1 mile.

events.title: Fall Colors Serenity Stroll
events.description: Meet at the West Picnic Area by the Rocky Point Trail trailhead.  Indulge your senses and rejuvenate your spirit surrounded by nature's rainbow of fall colors. Immerse yourself in tranquility as you embark on a guided journey designed to promote relaxation, mindfulness and well-being to celebrate the beginning of fall. We will be walking on the Rocky Point Trail up to the overlook of Lake Bemidji and back. This trail is paved and is a one-mile loop. Wear comfortable shoes. Meet in the west picnic area by the Rocky Point Trail trailhead. Look for the blue "program today" flag.

events.title: Measure the Potholes with a Naturalist
events.description: What lives inside a glacial pothole? How do you measure how deep one is? Is each one the same? Join the park naturalist to try simple experiments and measurements to discover these answers and more on a short 1/4-mile walk. This is a great guided walk for ages 5 and up, with chances for making guesses and hands-on activities. Meet outside the park's visitor center. This program takes place entirely outdoors and will be canceled or postponed in the event of lightning or thunder.

events.title: The Great Beak Match-up: Investigation Station
events.description: Big, small, long, or short, a bird's beak is a tool that helps it survive. So many different styles exist in nature. Drop-by with the park naturalist to discover a few of them in this hands-on matching activity with replica bird beaks. Most participants spend about ten minutes at this ongoing activity station. Find this station along the flat sidewalk outside the visitor center. Canceled in the event of rain.

events.title: Conversation Circle for English Language Learners
events.description: Conversation Circle is a casual gathering of English-language adult learners who meet at the library to practice their speaking skills in a group setting with help from an English-speaking volunteer. No need to register; just come when you can.

events.description: Since they first came on the market, e-bikes have been proven that they’re more than a fad. Electric bikes are faster and less physically taxing to operate than a normal bicycle but are also more complicated to maintain and more expensive for the casual consumer. Presented by Spencer Wolens, owner of of Pioneer Cycle in Blaine, this presentation will cover the types of e-bikes, reliable vendors for buying and maintaining an e-bike, safety advice and recommendations, and answer questions from attendees to help you decide if an e-bike works for you. events.description: The Anoka County Law Library hosts a criminal expungement clinic on the third Tuesday of each month.   No pre-registration is necessary.  Expungement is the process of filing a motion in court to request that a judge seal a court record. People request expungement when they have been denied employment, housing, or a professional license due to a criminal incident that appears on a background check. events.title: Let's Make Stuff: Nerikomi Dishes
events.description:
Join us for Let's Make Stuff! to get crafty and learn something new. Jump into the extraordinary world of Nerikomi in this fun introductory program! Nerikomi is the Japanese art of creating patterns using different colored clay bodies. Our teaching artist will provide colored clay bodies, molds, techniques, and special tips to help you create one-of-a-kind, hand-built dishes. In Europe, it's commonly called agateware. Whatever you call it, it's truly stunning.

This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund.

Let's Make Stuff! is a creative class for adults.

events.description:
For ages 18  Join us for a presentation on Feathers: A beautiful look at a bird's most unique feature by wildlife photographer Stan Tekiela

Every bird is covered with thousands of feathers. Each of these feathers is a combination of incredible engineering and absolute beauty. Feathers help birds keep cool on hot summer days, warm on cold winter nights, and they protect birds from harmful ultraviolet light from the sun.
