As we near the end of a lovely summer and before autumn brings its chill, come indulge your senses and rejuvenate your spirit with a wellness nature walk. Immerse yourself in the tranquility of the forest as you embark on a guided journey designed to promote relaxation, mindfulness and well-being.

We will be walking on the Paul Bunyan State Trail to the Sundew Pond Trail and back. This trail is paved and we will be walking about two miles. Wear comfortable shoes.

Meet at the picnic tables next to the marina. Look for the blue program f

events.title: Smokey the Beaver
events.description: Stop by the Visitor Center to learn about beavers and their incredible adaptations that allow them to build dams and create wetlands. Discover how these wetlands support wildlife, improve water storage, and can even help slow the spread of wildfires.

events.title: Kids Explorer Club Nature Hike
events.description:
Kids Explorer Club: Nature Hike Adventure

Join us for a fun outdoor adventure with the Kids Explorer Club! As we walk along the Pigeon River, we'll use our binoculars and dip nets to explore the wonders of nature. We'll look for birds, insects, wildflowers, and seek out river water creatures along the shoreline.

Along the way, we'll practice our observation skills by listening, watching, and discovering the amazing plants and animals that live around us. Bring your walking shoes and a sense of adventure!

events.title: Summer Nature Art for Kids
events.description:
Meet in the Visitor Center.

Come out the park and get creative! Kids of all ages will make art and crafts inspired by the outdoors using natural materials. This program encourages curiosity and a love of nature through hands-on art and exploration.

Stop by any time between 2 p.m. and 3:30 p.m. Meet in the Visitor Center.

events.title: Animal Skulls!
events.description: Can you tell the difference between an herbivore, omnivore, or carnivore just by looking at their teeth? Would you know which species you are looking at? Stop by the Visitor Center to learn how to tell skulls apart and guess which animals' skulls we have out!

events.title: Shovel Point - Guided Hike
events.description: Take a hike with a Naturalist out to Shovel Point and enjoy panoramic views of Lake Superior and its shoreline. We�ll discuss the fiery formation of this landscape, some of the plants and animals that make this harsh climate their home. The hike is 1.5 miles long and will meet at the Visitor Center. Bring sunscreen and sturdy shoes!

events.title: Old Timer's Cabin and the Civilian Conservation Corps
events.description:
Held at the Old Timer's Cabin, located along the boardwalk of Dr. Roberts Trail, below Douglas Lodge.

Only 4 (massive) logs tall, learn more about this Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) constructed building as well as what life was like in the CCC. Feel free to stop by at your leisure.

events.title: Jr. Naturalist: Animal Defenses
events.description:
Meet at the campfire circle outside the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds.

Stripes, smells, and quills! Kids, come investigate the many defenses that animals have to help them survive in their habitats. Create your own animal with its special defenses.

events.title: Meet the Snake! (great for all ages)
events.description:
Come say hello to a hog-nosed snake. A snake-enthusiast will be on hand to answer questions about the snakes of Minnesota. You may even gain an appreciation for these frequently misunderstood creatures. Most people spend 10 minutes at this station.

To meet the snake, drop by the Nature Play Area (see park map) anytime during the program.

events.title: A Microscopic World (great for all ages)
events.description:
Zoom in on tiny creatures and nature objects using the park's microscope. The image is projected onto a large screen. A naturalist will guide you in discovering the small, mysterious world that's all around us.

Drop by the air-conditioned Visitor Center anytime during the program. Most people spend about 10 minutes at this station. Seating available.

events.title: Meet the Snake! (great for all ages)
events.description:

events.title: Bats Eat Bugs (great for all ages)
events.description:
2026 is Bat Year at Wild River State Park. Join the naturalist for a special program with activities, games and stories that celebrate the eight species of bats in Minnesota. We'll take a twenty-minute bat walk in the middle of the program on a flat, paved trail. This program is designed for kids and adults.

Meet at the visitor center at the start time. Seating is available.

events.title: Bird Migration Walk (best for ages 8 to adult)
events.description:
Whether you've never birded before or you can identify all Minnesota species by ear, this walk is for you! We'll share our observations and questions and use our group's knowledge to better understand the birds around us. Bring binoculars and a field guide if you have them, or borrow ours. This walk will cover up to a mile.

Meet at the Visitor Center at the start time. Leave an extra 10 minutes to drive to the visitor center parking lot and walk to the building. Best for ages 8 to adult, but younger kids are welcome!

events.title: "How Do Birds Find Their Way?"- Story Time
events.description:
Migration fascinates us and is one of natures true wonders. The trip to their winter homes has already begun for many of our species and many more are gearing up for the journey. We will explore birds and their migration through story and hands-on-activities, so flap your way over to the visitor center for this pre-school age (2-6) story time program your little ones are sure to enjoy! Meet at the Visitor Center.

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

events.title: Hidden Treasures- Geocaching 101
events.description:
Join the naturalist to learn about geocaching, a real-life treasure hunt! We will be using GPS units to guide our way from one hidden treasure to the next. Learn the basics before putting your new knowledge to the test. All tools needed for this hunt will be provided. Meet at the Visitor Center.

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

Programs and events may be canceled due to inclement weather.

A park vehicle pass is required to enter the park and can be purchased at the park office. $35/annual or $7/day.

events.title: I Can Paddle! Canoeing
events.description:
These programs teach the basics of canoeing, from launching a canoe to paddling efficiently and planning a safe canoe outing.

This program requires a fee and pre-registration. To learn more go to https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state_parks/ican/paddle.html.

events.title: Marvelous Monarchs and Tagging:  Drop-in Nature Table
events.description:
Flying across the road, flitting in your backyard, or feeding on a flower while you are in the park, our state butterfly is busy this time of year. Monarchs have begun for their fall journey to Mexico. We will attempt to tag a few and release them. Drop by the main office to explore the marvelous monarchs!

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

Programs and events may be canceled due to inclement weather.

A park vehicle pass is required to enter the park and can be purchased at the park office. $35/annual or $7/day.

events.title: Birds and Birding Walk
events.description:
Birds are busy already starting migration while others are finishing raising babies or finding food, but it can be a hard time of year to spot them in the leaves and cover. Enjoy a short program on birds before learning some birding tips. We will then head out on a easy 40 minute walk where we will explore which birds are making all those chirps, tweets and toodle-dees. This is great for beginning birders and all wanting to enjoy the birds of the park. Meet at the Visitor Center.

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

Programs and events may be canceled due to inclement weather.

events.title: Meet the Trees
events.description:
Come learn about the trees. We'll be taking a short walk to learn about some of the trees in our area and then return to the Interpretive Center Classroom to make a unique leaf rubbing picture.

We will be meeting at the Interpretive Center and walking along a small portion of Pondview Interpretive Trail.

events.title: Fabulous Frogs- Story Time
events.description:
From life in the water to life on land, frogs have some amazing superpowers that include winter survival. Join us to learn more about frogs as we explore these amazing creatures during this hands-on program. The naturalist will read a story and guide participants on a frog hunt. There will be activities and a craft that your little "tadpoles." Meet at the Visitor Center.

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

Programs and events may be canceled due to inclement weather.

A park vehicle pass is required to enter the park and can be purchased at the park office. $35/annual or $7/day.

events.title: Terrific Trees and Tree I.D.
events.description:
Trees not only provide oxygen, they provide habitat for animals and products we use every day, like paper, pencils and lumber. While you might also enjoy the fall color or shade they provide, those leaves make trees much easier to identify. Come explore trees through hands-on activities, including tree identification. This is a family friendly program. Meet at the Visitor Center.

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

events.title: Birding for Beginners
events.description:
Want to try birding, but don't know where to start? Join the naturalist on the Pondview Trail to learn about some of the birds that call the area home.

For the best experience, binoculars are recommended. Please bring your own binoculars if you have them. We have a limited number of binoculars available for those who do not have their own. Please ask the naturalist to borrow a pair when you arrive for the hike if needed.

We will be meeting at the Sibley Interpretive Center and hiking the Pondview Interpretive Trail. It is a 0.7-mile loop with a maximum grade of 7 percent for 190ft.

events.title: Fish Prints
events.description:
Fish Printing was developed in Japan. It was used by fisherman to record their catches before cameras were available. Over time it became its own unique artform.

Drop by the interpreter's table at the beach to make a fish print and learn a little bit about some of the fish that reside in Lake Andrew.

Activity lasts about 5 minutes.

events.title: Get Hooked on Fishing
events.description:
Come learn the basics of fishing and what you can expect to catch in the lake.

The program is designed with beginners and ages 6-11 in mind, but all are welcome to participate. Minors must be accompanied by an adult. All equipment is provided.

This program is limited to 10 fishing participants. Please pre-register by contacting Savannah at: savannah.stephenson@state.mn.us

Pre-registration ends at 3:00 p.m. on Saturday, September 5.

We will be meeting at the fishing pier at the Beach.

events.title: Tall Tale Trivia
events.description:
There are a lot of myths surrounding nature. Can you distinguish fact from fiction? Join a naturalist to play a game of trivia and figure out the facts about the world around us.

We will be meeting in the classroom in the downstairs area of the Interpretive Center.

events.title: A Morning on the Oak Savanna
events.description:
Oak Savannas are a rare, special type of prairie that support an amazing ecosystem, and you can find it right here in the park. Come explore the habitat and learn what makes it special.

We will be meeting at the Sibley Interpretive Center and hiking the Pondview Interpretive Trail. It is a 0.7-mile loop with a maximum grade of 7% over 190ft.

events.title: Bird Search for Kids
events.description:
Join the naturalist on a family-friendly adventure to hunt for bird plushes around the Interpretive Center and Amphitheater. Along the way we will talk about what makes the birds special, key traits to look at for identification, and stop to look at the live birds that frequent the area. This activity is designed for ages 4-6, but all are welcome to participate.

We will be meeting at the Interpretive Center.

events.title: Aquatic Adventure
events.description:
Meet at the William H. Morrissey Visitor Center at Mystery Cave

Step into the South Branch Root River and discover the incredible world of the animals living beneath the surface. During this hands‑on adventure, you�ll search for a variety of aquatic invertebrates�like caddisfly, mayfly, and stonefly larvae�and get an up‑close look at how they thrive in moving water. Plan to wade in knee‑deep currents as you sample and observe these fascinating river residents. Sandals with a heel strap, tennis shoes, or water shoes are required to protect your feet.

events.title: Bats Eat Bugs (great for all ages)
events.description:
2026 is Bat Year at Wild River State Park. Join the naturalist for a special program with activities, games and stories that celebrate the eight species of bats in Minnesota. We'll take a twenty-minute bat walk in the middle of the program on a flat, paved trail. This program is designed for kids and adults.

Meet at the visitor center at the start time. Seating is available.

events.title: Bird Migration Walk (best for ages 8 to adult)
events.description:
Whether you've never birded before or you can identify all Minnesota species by ear, this walk is for you! We'll share our observations and questions and use our group's knowledge to better understand the birds around us. Bring binoculars and a field guide if you have them, or borrow ours. This walk will cover up to a mile.

Meet at the Visitor Center at the start time. Leave an extra 10 minutes to drive to the visitor center parking lot and walk to the building. Best for ages 8 to adult, but younger kids are welcome!

events.title: Almelund Apple Festival - 3 miles from the park
events.description:
The park naturalists and Friends of Wild River State Park will be at the Alemelund Apple Festival. Come say hello and make a free buckthorn walking stick to take home. Pet a live snake that's an ambassador for real snakes that live at the park. Enjoy many other festivities at this community celebration.

The Almelund Apple Festival runs from 11-4 and is located in the town of Almelund, just 3 miles from the park. Entrance to the festival is free.

events.title: Birds of Wild River (best for ages 3 to adult)
events.description:
What's that flying overhead? It's a bird! Stop by to learn some basic bird identification skills, and to explore some of the over 200 species of birds that visit Wild River State Park every year! This program is fun for both kids and adults and includes a short activity to put your bird observation skills to the test.

This drop-in station will be available at Visitor Center.

events.title: Morning Nature Walk (all ages)
events.description:
Start your day on the right foot. Stroll a mile with a park naturalist while stopping to appreciate natural curiosities along the way. The flat trail is a mixture of packed earth and mowed grass, with a few stretches of sand.

Meet at the overflow parking lot at the campground, between the D and E lanes. The walk will start right at 8, so please be on time.

events.description: Join us online for an evening with author, David Heska Wanbli Weiden. David Heska Wanbli Weiden is an enrolled citizen of the Sicangu Lakota nation and a leading Indigenous voice in the crime fiction and thriller genres. In his chart-topping debut Winter Counts (2020), Weiden introduces Virgil Wounded Horse, a vigilante enforcer on a South Dakota reservation who steps up to root out a drug ring after formal legal systems fail his community. Winter Counts practically swept the mystery genre’s literary honors, winning an Anthony Award, Lefty Award, ITW Thriller Award, Barry Award, and Macavity A

events.title: Old Timer's Cabin, Open Tour
events.description: Held at the Old Timer's Cabin, located along the boardwalk below Douglas Lodge. Only 4 (massive) logs tall, learn more about this Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) constructed building. The Naturalist staff will have the cabin open for you to tour at your leisure.

events.title: Five Facts in Five Minutes: Beavers
events.description: Near the Mississippi Headwaters (at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center if rain.) Only have a minute to learn about Itasca State Park? Check out a unique feature at the naturalist station as you visit the Headwaters of the Mississippi River.

events.title: Nature Walk with a Park Ranger
events.description: Nature walk with park manager Jake Gaster. Ranger Jake will lead visitors along trails through the upland area of the park, pointing out a variety of natural features as they are encountered. Dress for the weather and bring sun and tick protection. Meet at the shower building in the campground.

events.title: Manoomin: Wild Rice Walk
events.description: Meet at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center. Interested in our Minnesota state grain? Have you ever eaten wild rice and wondered where it came from? Join us as we walk to the Headwaters of the Mississippi River and talk about wild rice, manoomin in Ojibwe. Come see �the good berry� and learn how it is traditionally harvested and processed.

events.title: Mississippi Headwaters Mysteries Walk
events.description: Meet at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center. Did you ever wonder: How did Lake Itasca get its name? Have those rocks always been there? Does the river ever freeze? Discover the answer to these mysteries about the Mississippi River and Lake Itasca as we walk to the headwaters.

events.title: Fall Leaves Bike Ride
events.description: Meet at the parking lot of the Itasca Sports Rental. Like to ride bike? Interested in learning about the trees of Itasca? Bring your bike and head down the trail with a Naturalist as we explore colorful fall leaves and the trees that they belong to.

events.title: Got Elk?
events.description: Meet at the Lake Itasca Amphitheater in the picnic grounds (if raining meet inside Forest Inn, across from Douglas Lodge). Did you know that there used to be elk at Itasca State Park? Where did these elk come from and where did they go? Come find out at the Itasca amphitheater! In this program, we will learn about elk as mammals and some of the efforts to reintroduce elk into the park. We will end with a walk to a historic elk site!

events.description: Find the meditative power of hand sewing, learn the history of the craft, and lessen your consumption by repairing your own clothes! events.title: Seed Saving and Keeping / Guardado y conservación de semillas
events.description: We can all be seed keepers! Saving seeds helps us adapt to our changing climate. Plants have a working memory. Each growing season they experience the environment like we do! The plants remember what the season was like and code that information into their seeds for the next year! When you save seeds and plant them the next season (and repeat!) we cultivate plants that are uniquely adapted to our local region and help to ensure food sovereignty for our future. Join seed keeper Charly for a seed-saving walk through the library garden! Spanish interpretation provided. ¡Todos podemos ser guardian

events.title: Protection Charm With Traditional Korean Patchwork
events.description: These classes center on the theme, "The Art of Being With...," and are related to the exhibit at Minneapolis Central Library. Together, they explore the idea that giving and receiving care and love brings meaning to our lives. Thoughtfulness is essential in finding purpose; without it, everyday moments can feel less significant. Rather than focusing on technical skills, each class highlights the meaningful act of creating objects that reflect care. Participants will work with ceramic painting and traditional textile elements to practice thoughtfulness and express care for themselves and others

events.title: Botanical Monotype
events.description: Learn how to make your own monotype, a unique, one-of-a-kind print, using botanicals! Artist Diana Eicher will teach you how to ink up botanicals and plant materials, transfer plants to a plexiglass plate, paint with inks, and print designs using a printing press to make a one-color print to take home. Materials provided. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund. Diana Eicher is the Director of the Printmaking and Paper Studio at the Minneapolis College of Art and Design. She is a visual artist working at the intersection of identity, lived experience

events.title: Writing as a Profession: Buried Bias in Craft
events.description: How can we better adapt our writing habits to accommodate diversity in myriad forms? Explore the complexity of narrative when writing outside of one’s lived experience and personal identity via a candid discussion about what an unapologetic, anti-racist approach to writing looks like. events.title: Writing as a Profession: Literary Agents: What to Look For and What to Look Out For
events.description: Most publishers won’t look at your prose manuscript unless an agent represents you. So how do you get an agent? Learn what good agents do and don’t do, and how to find the right one for your work along with the basics of writing a query letter. Part of a four-part series, “Writing as a Profession.” Attendance at all four sessions not required. Collaborator: The Loft Literary Center. events.title: Bloomington Water Lantern Festival by Light The Night
events.description:
Experience the enchantment of a magical evening at our Water Lantern Festival! Join us as we gather by the water’s edge to celebrate love, hope, and dreams, all illuminated by the gentle glow of floating lanterns.

As the sun begins to set, you’ll be captivated by the serene beauty of the scene. Each participant will receive a beautifully crafted lantern to personalize with their wishes, dreams, or messages of love. Together, we will release these lanterns onto the water, creating a breathtaking display of floating lights that reflect upon the tranquil surface.

Immerse yourself in the peaceful ambiance as you watch the lanterns dance upon the water, carrying with them the hopes and aspirations of all who participate. The soft glow and gentle ripples create a serene atmosphere, perfect for reflection and connection.

Our Water Lantern Festival is a celebration of unity, community, and shared experiences. It’s an opportunity to come together with friends, family, and strangers alike, to embrace the magic of the moment and create lasting memories.

Whether you’re seeking a romantic evening, a moment of tranquility, or simply a unique experience, this festival promises a captivating and unforgettable journey. Join us as we ignite the water’s surface with light, love, and dreams, and let the beauty of floating lanterns leave you in awe.

events.title: Nuss Collection Fall Museum Open House – Rochester, MN
events.description:
Join us for The Nuss Collection 2026 Open House, an homage to the essence of American craftsmanship and ingenuity. Step into a captivating journey through time as we showcase meticulously restored and preserved historical trucks, each representing the backbone of America’s growth and development.

Date: September 19, 2026
Time: 9 a.m. – 3 p.m.

Experience the evolution of trucking, from the early 1900s to today, with a remarkable lineup of vehicles that shaped the nation. This year’s event will honor 125 years of Mack Trucks, celebrating more than a century of groundbreaking design and innovation. Discover the fascinating stories behind these iconic machines and their enduring impact on American history.

Adding to the celebration, immerse yourself in the work of renowned artist Bob Evans, whose decades-long collaboration with Mack Trucks brought their heritage to life. His extraordinary acrylic paintings—featured in Mack calendar art and Christmas cards—will be on display, offering a unique visual tribute to Mack’s legacy.

Admission is free, and all are welcome to enjoy a day filled with history, incredible trucks, and delicious food and refreshments. Be part of this celebration of American heritage and innovation at The Nuss Collection 2026 Open House!

#NussCollection2026 #Mack125 #AmericanCraftsmanship #MackTrucks #VolvoTrucks #TruckHistory #NussOpenHouse

events.title: Booked on Thursdays: "An Eye for an I: Growing up with Blindness, Bigotry, and Family Mental Illness
events.description:
Join the Minnesota Historical Society’s Inclusion and Community Engagement team for a new event series, Booked on Thursdays! All are welcome to join us, get to know each other, and share reflections on a curated list of books by local Minnesota authors. Stories featured will emphasize themes of community resilience, resistance, and joy.

Whether you read a few pages, a few chapters, or finish the book, all are invited to participate. Each session will be an informal space to connect with people with shared interests related to the book themes and to learn about resources related to the history of communities and themes featured in the selected book. Our featured book this month is An Eye for an I: Growing up with Blindness, Bigotry, and Family Mental Illness by James Francisco Bonilla.

If you would like to request a free copy of a book included in the reading list, please email engagement@mnhs.org after you register. We will have limited copies available upon request.

Planning your visit to the Minnesota History Center

Free Minnesota History Center admission and parking is available every Thursday from 4-8 pm. Attendees are invited to explore the exhibits available on the 3rd floor before the start of the event. Directions to the Minnesota History Center can be found on the museum website. To request an accommodation or for inquiries about accessibility, please contact engagement@mnhs.org.

events.title: Children & Family Weekend: Loft Poetry Workshop/youth
events.description:
FOR THE LOVE OF THE GAME
poetry workshop, ages 13-17

"With a bolt of lightning on my kicks . . .The court is SIZZLING. My sweat is DRIZZLING. Stop all that quivering. Cuz tonight I’m delivering,"

-The Crossover, Kwame Alexander 2015

Whether you're racing down the soccer pitch, nailing a dance solo, or hitting that field goal with a swish, there's something so special about killing it at the activities you love.

But how can we put words to that exceptional feeling? How can we share with others what it means to be in that moment, with adrenaline rushing and muscle memory carrying you to success?

This class is designed especially for young people aged 13 - 17 to express their love of the game in fun, genuine ways that match the energy they feel in their favorite sport or activity. Join author and educator Dralandra Larkins at Hope Arts Center from 2 - 3:30 p.m. for a class you won't forget!

About the educator:

Dralandra Larkins is an award-winning educator, spoken-word poet, and author of Before I Lie. She serves as Lead Poetry Mentor for the Minnesota Humanities Center’s Minnesota Youth Poet Laureate program, Artistic Director for the Minnesota Black Authors Expo Executive Committee, and a COMPAS teaching artist. A recipient of the Loft Literary Center Teaching Artist Fellowship, her work has been presented by the Minneapolis Institute of Art, NAACP, Minnesota State Capitol, St. Cloud State University, and Hennepin County Library, and featured by Minnesota Public Radio,

events.title: SBR: Marketing Matters... No Really. It Does.
events.description:
September Topic: Marketing Matters - Website SEO

Let's be honest—marketing can feel overwhelming. Algorithms change (every day), trends come and go, and everyone's got an opinion on what you should be doing.

So let's cut through the noise. This session is designed to be practical, conversational, and immediately useful.

Whether you're a one-person marketing department, a business owner wearing every hat, or part of a larger team, you'll leave with practical ideas, fresh perspective, and actionable takeaways you can implement immediately.

Here's what to expect:

10 minutes of expert insight featuring one focused marketing topic, strategy, or best practice you can put into action right away.

Open discussion where we dive deeper into the topic together.
Real conversations with tablemates about what's actually working (and what isn't).
Peer-to-peer learning from fellow business owners and marketing professionals facing the same challenges.

Demystifying the "why" behind successful marketing strategies.
Honest conversations about social media—where the real needle-movers are, what's worth your time, and what you can stop stressing over.
Because marketing doesn't have to be complicated.

No, really. It doesn't.

events.title: The Leading Edge FTO | St. Paul, MN
events.description:
About This Course
Field Training Officers (FTOs) serve in one of the most critical roles of any organization. Beyond training new or lateral officers, they are key in building organizational culture. Sadly, a greater emphasis is often on evaluating and documenting, rather than training. The Leading Edge FTO intentionally challenges “the way we’ve always done it.” The real goal should be to train and mentor the next generation of officers to serve their communities successfully.

Through guided discussion, case study, and video analysis, participants will explore the following: 
Understand the role of the FTO as a trainer, not just an evaluator 
Understand the role of the FTO as an agency leader 
Explore how FTOs can become better coaches and mentors 
Understand FTO accountability; for themselves, the trainee, and the agency 
Understand documentation: what great agencies do that others don’t 
‍
Appropriate Audience
This course is designed for current or prospective FTO’s/ CTO’s, FTO/CTO Program Supervisors, and Training Unit Managers.

‍Course Length
16 hours

events.title: Spirits of Summit Avenue St. Paul Ghost Walk
events.description:
🕯️👻 Spirits of Summit Avenue: St. Paul Ghost Walk 👻🕯️
📍 239 Selby Ave, St. Paul, MN 55102
⏱️ 90 Minutes | $34.21 per person (includes all taxes + fees)
👤 Ages 13+
⸻
Step into the shadows of St. Paul’s most elegant — and eerie — street. Summit Avenue, once home to Gilded Age millionaires and powerful industrialists, is lined with opulent mansions that hold more than just history within their walls.
This 90-minute walking tour blends stunning architecture with real ghost stories, eerie legends, and paranormal accounts pulled straight from the headlines.
In 1969, a séance in the infamous Griggs Mansion ended with journalists swearing they would never return alone. Apparitions. Footsteps. Knocks on the walls. And the chilling conclusion:
“There is no prize on earth that could get us to spend a single night alone in that great stone house.”
Now it’s your turn to hear the stories… and feel the atmosphere for yourself.
⸻
🔮 What You’ll Experience:
• The haunted halls of the James J. Hill House
• The tragic ghost of Molly at Forepaugh’s Mansion
• The mysterious past of the William Butler House
• Legendary madame Nina Clifford
• Local stories of aviation pioneer Amelia Earhart, spiritualism, and unsolved mysteries
Led by expert storyteller Dangerous Linda, this tour is not just about ghosts — it’s about the souls of the city, the secrets of its stone walls, and the history that still lingers in the night air.
⸻
👟 Easy-to-moderate walking
🦽 Wheelchair accessible (let us know in advance)

events.title: Children & Family Weekend: Erin Walsh
events.description:
Erin Walsh offers a special presentation titled “It’s Their World: Raising Resilient Kids  in the Digital Age"

*This talk is recommended for adults: parents, grandparents, caregivers, educators, mentors, health professionals, adults interested in the intersection of technology and health, and all those who care about nurturing our community’s younger generation. Simultaneous to this presentation, for children and youth, we offer poetry workshops with The Loft Literary Center. 

 
Erin Walsh is co-founder of Spark & Stitch Institute and author of It’s Their World: Teens, Screens, and the Science of Adolescence. She has worked with communities across the country who want to better understand child and adolescent development and cut through conflicting information about kids and technology. Her work has been featured in the Washington Post, Edutopia, Parents.com, Psychology Today, and Minnesota Public Radio. She co-authored the Tenth Anniversary Edition of the national bestseller Why Do They Act That Way? A Survival Guide to the Adolescent Brain for You and Your Teen and has worked with schools, school districts, parent groups and other youth serving organizations throughout the United States and Canada on issues related to digital media, parenting, and child and adolescent development. You can follow her work at sparkandstitchinstitute.com.

events.title: Children & Family Weekend: Kwame Alexander
events.description:
A poetry reading and conversation with Kwame Alexander.
Guest moderator, Arleta Little of the Loft Literary Center.

Kwame Alexander is a poet, educator, Emmy-winning producer, and #1 New York Times bestselling author of more than 40 books, including The Crossover, The Undefeated, Becoming Muhammad Ali, The Door of No Return, and This Is the Honey. His acclaimed work has earned numerous honors, including the Newbery Medal, Caldecott Medal, and National Book Award recognition. He is also the Emmy-winning executive producer, showrunner, and writer of Disney+'s The Crossover, produced in partnership with LeBron James' SpringHill Company. Through his production company, Big Sea Entertainment, he creates innovative children's and family programming that promotes literacy and storytelling. A frequent speaker and contributor to NPR, Kwame shares his passion for reading and writing with audiences around the world. His mission is simple: to change the world, one word at a time.

events.title: Still Here: Navigating Life while Grieving
events.description:
Grief isn’t limited to the loss of a loved one. Sometimes we grieve the end of a relationship, the loss of a dream, a miscarriage, infertility, a career, our health, childhood experiences, friendships, financial stability, a major life transition, or even the version of ourselves we no longer recognize.

If you’ve ever felt like life expected you to move on before your heart was ready, this workshop was created with you in mind.

Still Here: Navigating Life While Grieving is a compassionate and supportive healing experience designed to help you better understand grief, honor your emotions, and learn practical ways to care for yourself while navigating life’s most difficult seasons.

Together, we will explore:

Understanding the many forms of grief
How grief impacts the mind, body, and spirit
The emotional stages of grief—and why healing isn’t always linear
Healthy ways to process difficult emotions without suppressing them
Practical coping tools for everyday life
Grounding and breathing techniques to calm the nervous system
Journaling and reflection exercises for emotional release
Rebuilding hope, purpose, and self-compassion after loss
Finding permission to experience joy again without guilt
This is not a space where you’ll be expected to “be okay.” This is a space where you are welcome to come exactly as you are.

Whether your grief is fresh or you’ve been carrying it quietly for years, you’ll leave with greater understanding, practical tools, and the reminder that healing

events.description:
Friday, September 4 - Saturday, September 5, 2026 
9a - 4p daily
Tuition: $250 [MMAM member rate: $240]
Register: https://mmam.org/calendar2/workshop-ducett


Are you curious about Third Street? We are too.

The Center for Third Street Furtherings (CfTSF) has been active in Winona for some time now—quietly observing, recording, and assembling a clearer picture of a place that resists easy definition. In partnership with the Minnesota Marine Art Museum, the Center is now accepting a limited cohort of Field Agent Trainees to assist with an active investigation led by Senior Collection Agent Andy DuCett.

Your assignment begins with onboarding.

Over two days, you will be trained in a series of CfTSF-approved methodologies developed in alignment with DuCett’s artistic practice. These include:

** Close Observation Protocols
Learn to register the overlooked: signage, residue, patterns of movement, unofficial histories.

**Applied Cartographic Drift
Working in the lineage of Denis Wood, participants will construct subjective, data-rich maps that privilege experience over cartographic accuracy.

** Speculative Collection Techniques
You will gather and catalog physical and visual “evidence” from the field—ephemera, fragments, images, and notes.

** Document Fabrication + Narrative Assembly
Transform your findings into CfTSF-sanctioned outputs: broadsides, annotated diagrams, fictionalized reports, and micro-publications.

Tickets: https://mmam.org/calendar2/2026-third-thursday-sept-author

Join us for an evening of conversation, connection, and community as award-winning authors Anna Farro Henderson and Tamara Dean take the stage alongside local community voices for a timely discussion on climate, creativity, and collective action. Through their acclaimed essay collections, Core Samples: A Climate Scientist’s Experiments in Motherhood and Politics and Shelter and Storm: At Home in the Driftless, Henderson and Dean weave science, policy, and personal experience into powerful reflections on our relationship to the natural world and one another.

This engaging program explores how art, storytelling, and community can help us navigate climate anxiety and imagine meaningful change. Community organizations will also host booths where guests can learn more about local climate issues, clean energy, healthy soils, and ways to get involved close to home. Discover how turning toward each other may be the most powerful response to an uncertain future.

About the authors:

Tamara Dean is a widely published author whose latest book, Shelter and Storm: At Home in the Driftless (University of Minnesota Press, 2025), invites readers to step into the Driftless Area

Past, Present & Future Bar Bingo, a rousing gallery game inspired by Winona’s history and the places. The game invites participants to move between the museum and the city of Winona, past and present, and familiar places in Winona.

On September 12, join MMAM exhibiting artist, Andy DuCett in his exhibition "Home(town)" for Past, Present & Future Bar Bingo. The game begins with an original piece of Winona history: the Bingo board from the former Winona Athletic Club. Andy will be calling traditional bingo in the galleries with Winona bar tokens as markers. Make sure to pick up your prize before exploring "Home(town)!" 

Players can keep their bingo cards and use them to play the present and future portions of Past, Present & Future Bar Bingo. Playing Past Bingo is the only way to earn your card to play Present and Future Bingo. Attend a Bingo session at MMAM to learn about the next steps! 

Come for the art, stay for the game, and see where "Home(town)" takes you.

events.description:

Fall is quickly approaching at Caponi Art Park and we’re thrilled to host composer and director JG Everest’s Sound Garden. 

The Sound Garden at Caponi is a temporary installation at Caponi Art Park that builds on the existing natural soundscape throughout the park and immerses its audience using carefully designed music, dance, poetry, and visual art. 

Open daily from noon – 4:00 PM. Guided tours available on weekends.

𝗙𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗔𝗿𝘁 + 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗽𝘀 𝗮𝘁 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗶
𝗦𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿 𝟭𝟮, 𝟭𝟵, 𝟮𝟲, 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲

Join us for a series of free workshops and special events that invite visitors of all ages to connect with art, nature, and community in meaningful ways. From writing poetry inspired by nature to creating natural sculptures, exploring sound and music, and experiencing the immersive Sound Garden installation, there's something for everyone to enjoy. 

Learn more on our website >> https://www.caponiartpark.org/events/fallsoundgarden2026/

𝗩𝗼𝗹𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗡𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗲𝗱!

Be part of the creation of a brand new, large-scale public artwork — help Caponi Art Park prepare for the 2026 Sound Garden.

events.title: Restore Caponi: Buckthorn Removal Workshop With Friends of the Mississippi River
events.description:
𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗮𝘆, 𝗦𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿 𝟮𝟴 | 𝟰:𝟬𝟬–𝟲:𝟬𝟬 𝗽.𝗺.

Join Friends of the Mississippi River for a hands-on volunteer workshop focused on removing invasive buckthorn using Critical Period Cutting—an effective, herbicide-free method for controlling mature buckthorn. 

You'll learn why this technique works, how it supports healthy forests and native habitats, and then put your new skills into practice alongside fellow volunteers.

Whether you're passionate about conservation or simply looking for a meaningful way to give back, this is a great opportunity to make a lasting impact on the park while learning from restoration experts.

Learn about invasive buckthorn and its impact on Minnesota's woodlands.

Receive hands-on instruction from Friends of the Mississippi River staff.

Practice the Critical Period Cutting method in areas of Caponi Art Park undergoing ecological restoration.

Help improve wildlife habitat and support the park's long-term restoration efforts.

No previous experience is necessary. All training, tools, and supplies will be provided.

Work gloves will be provided, but you're welcome to bring your own if you prefer.

volunteer_opportunities.description: Volunteers 16+ help create play experiences for children and families. Assist with programs, events, cleaning and prep work. Group volunteering available from businesses and community organizations.

volunteer_opportunities.description: Family meal packing volunteer opportunity at FMSC Chanhassen. Pack nutritious meals in a fun, group-friendly environment. Serves southwest Twin Cities metro area.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Feed My Starving Children - Eagan Meal Packing
volunteer_opportunities.description: Pack MannaPack meals with family members at FMSC Eagan location. Each 2-hour shift packs approximately $60 worth of meals. Suitable for families and groups.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Twin Cities Habitat for Humanity - Family Volunteer
volunteer_opportunities.description: Non-construction volunteer roles for youth and families. Cookie Baker activity (no age requirement, at-home). ReStore volunteer (must be at least 14 years old). Help build homes for families in need.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Minnesota DNR Park & Trail Volunteer Program
volunteer_opportunities.description: Families can volunteer to improve and maintain Minnesota's natural areas, state parks, forests, and wildlife areas. No minimum hourly requirement; typical projects are 1.5-3 hours.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Saint Paul Citywide Summer Cleanup
volunteer_opportunities.description: Family-friendly park cleanup volunteer events. Schedule a summer cleanup with the City of Saint Paul to pick up litter and beautify parks.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Minneapolis Park & Recreation Volunteer Cleanup
volunteer_opportunities.description: Litter picks and park/playground clean-up for volunteer groups. Submit request at least 3 weeks prior. Great way for families to contribute to their community.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Feed My Starving Children - Coon Rapids Meal Packing
volunteer_opportunities.description: Volunteer as a family to pack nutritious MannaPack meals (vitamins, vegetables, soy, rice) into bags and boxes for distribution to hungry children worldwide. Ages 5+, families welcome.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Second Harvest Heartland - Brooklyn Park Food Bank
volunteer_opportunities.description: Food bank volunteer opportunity welcoming families ages 8 and older to help pack and sort food items. Group volunteering available for 2+ people.

volunteer_opportunities.description: Build or rehab homes alongside families in the community. Youth (14-17) must have adult accompaniment. No construction experience required. Volunteer orientation available every other week.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Ronald McDonald House - Cooks for Kids Program
volunteer_opportunities.description: Groups prepare and serve meals to families at Ronald McDonald House locations. Monthly birthday parties available first Thursday 5-6pm with activities and cake. Meal sponsorship options year-round.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Bridging Minnesota - Warehouse Volunteer
volunteer_opportunities.description: Teams help sort donated furniture and household goods for families transitioning out of homelessness. Groups 5-25 volunteers, 2-3 hour shifts. Minimum age 14. Available Tuesdays-Thursdays after 1pm.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Sleep in Heavenly Peace - Bed Building
volunteer_opportunities.description: Build and assemble beds for children ages 3-17 in need. Families can participate in community bed build events. Children under 12 require parent supervision; 12+ need legal guardian accompaniment.

volunteer_opportunities.description: Family-friendly garden maintenance volunteer opportunity. Staff-led group meets twice weekly to care for the Peace Garden in Minneapolis parks.

volunteer_opportunities.description: Help seniors with yard work, lawn mowing, spring cleanup, and fall leaf raking. Family-friendly with kids age 7+. Minimum age 16 to volunteer alone; younger volunteers need parent supervision.

volunteer_opportunities.title: Children's Minnesota - Hospital Volunteer Programs
volunteer_opportunities.description: Read books to patients and siblings, assist at fundraisers, provide hospitality support, and help with patient activities. Opportunities for families and young volunteers interested in healthcare.
